title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is from the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes, an axiomatics of 'figures' with data (M, ≤, ≪, F) and axioms labelled At n. On p.48 Grothendieck wants a morphism f : F' → F of such structures to come from a canonical, surjective, order-preserving map φ : F̃ → F̃' (1.55). The induced map (1.54) on families of figures should then be recovered as A ↦ φ^{-1}(A) on closed parts (1.56). He notes that such a φ, when it exists, is unique; this page states and proves that uniqueness as a lemma.

Lemma (modern form). Let I, I' be ordered sets ('pré' is crossed out). Give each the Alexandrov topology whose closed sets are the down-sets, and let Pf(I) be the lattice of closed parts. The map Hom_incr(I, I') → Hom_incr(Pf(I'), Pf(I)), φ ↦ φ^{-1}, is injective: φ(i) is recovered as the least i' with i ∈ φ^{-1}(↓i').
- Its image is exactly the maps Pf(I') → Pf(I) that commute with arbitrary intersections and arbitrary unions. These are the complete-lattice homomorphisms between down-set lattices, i.e. the classical (Birkhoff–Raney) duality between posets and completely distributive algebraic lattices.
- He then weakens the condition, via a marginal note, to preserving arbitrary joins and finite meets. This is the frame-hom (locale) condition, so these maps correspond to geometric morphisms Top(I) → Top(I'), i.e. continuous maps I → Î', where Î' is the sobrification of I' (assuming I sober).
- For an Alexandrov space the irreducible closed sets are the directed down-sets (ideals), so Î' is the ideal completion of I'.
- The second marginal note says the strict (complete-lattice) maps are exactly those that send the closures of points i ∈ I to irreducible closed sets of the special form cl{i'} = I'_{≤ i'}. These give honest increasing maps I → I' and recover (1.55).

Next question. Is the order or topology on F̃ the inverse image of that on F̃' under φ? He states this is equivalent to surjectivity of (1.54).

Example. Take the 'trivial' choices (M, ≤, ≪ := ≤, F), as on p.44. Axiom At 8 then forces: every X has a minimal x ≤ X such that X is an immediate successor of x (when X ≠ x). Page 50 calls this very restrictive. With F = Pf(M) and F' = Pf(M'), the lemma shows morphisms are just arbitrary increasing maps M → M'. So the initial-topology / surjectivity condition is a genuine extra constraint.
errors: Injectivity fails for genuine preorders: maps differing by values in the same equivalence class have the same preimages on down-sets. Grothendieck's deletion of 'pré' fixes this.
The prose says 'applic. cr. de Pf(I) dans Pf(I')', but the displayed arrow and (*) run Pf(I') → Pf(I). This is a slip of direction.

The marginal 'commutent aux réunions quelconques, et aux intersections finies' is correct for lattices of opens. For the closed sets Pf it should be arbitrary intersections and finite unions. Either he silently passed to opens or it is a slip.

The topos/sobrification statement needs care. Frame maps O(I') → O(I) correspond to continuous maps from sob(I) to sob(I'); they reduce to maps I → Î' only when I is sober. For an Alexandrov space, sober means every ideal is principal, e.g. I finite or satisfying the ascending chain condition. He does add 'supposé I sobre'.

ideas.what: Increasing maps I → I' embed injectively into maps of down-set lattices via inverse image; the image is the maps preserving all unions and intersections.
ideas.modern_name: Duality between posets and completely distributive algebraic (Alexandrov) lattices; complete homomorphisms of down-set lattices
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (finite case), Raney (1950s), Alexandrov (1937) for the topology

ideas.what: Frame-type maps (arbitrary joins, finite meets) correspond to topos morphisms Top(I) → Top(I') and to continuous maps I → Î'.
ideas.modern_name: Localic/geometric morphisms between Alexandrov toposes; sobrification of an Alexandrov space = ideal completion
ideas.usually_credited_to: SGA4 (points of topoi, sober spaces); Johnstone, Stone Spaces (1982)
ideas.where_published: SGA4 Exp. IV (sober spaces, morphisms of topoi of spaces)

ideas.what: Complete-lattice maps are those sending point closures to principal irreducible closed sets I'_{≤i'}.
ideas.modern_name: Characterisation of 'principal' points in the ideal completion (compact elements)

ideas.what: Order on F̃ being the inverse image under φ is equivalent to surjectivity of (1.54); for trivial choices (≪ = ≤) axiom At 8 forces every element to be an immediate successor of a minimal one.
ideas.modern_name: Initial (induced) order / strict morphisms in an axiomatic tame topology of figures

missed.claim: Within the 1986 Analysis situs axiomatics, Grothendieck isolates which morphisms of 'figure' structures come from order-preserving maps of the associated posets F̃. He identifies the extra 'strictness' condition (initial order, i.e. surjectivity of (1.54)) as substantive. This belongs to his unpublished programme of an axiomatic tame topology, but the lemma itself is classical.
missed.quote: Mais avons-nous nécessairement que la top de F̃ est image inv. de celle de F̃'? En fait, c'est équivalent à la surjectivité de (1.54).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of interest mainly to historians reconstructing the 1986 'topologie modérée' axiomatics (axioms At n, figures Fig(L)). It gives no new mathematical result for specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: The page proves a standard Alexandrov/Birkhoff-type duality lemma and relates it to topos morphisms and sobrification, all well known. Only the surrounding axiomatics of figures is unpublished.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'Hom croiss' and 'Hom cr' are correct; the target is Hom_cr(Pf(I'), Pf(I)), i.e. contravariant.

'Son image est formée des [antécédents des]' likely reads 'Son image est formée des applications (*) Pf(I') → Pf(I) commutant aux intersections et réunions quelconques'. The insertion '{+antécédents des+}' looks doubtful.

In the margin, 'les transformant des strictes de I'' probably reads roughly 'Correspondent aux applications de Pf transformant les adhérences de points i ∈ I en des parties fermées irréductibles de la forme cl{i'} = I'_{≤i'}'.
Marginal 'comme I' supposé sobre, cela signifie que ... I' likely reads '...cela signifie que l'application provient d'une application croissante I → I''.
